sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} qualifies only if ALL of these conditions hold for it:

rules.text: At least one {{entity_noun}} can be identified from the phrase and its relationship summary.

children.text: The category must actually be determinable. A phrase that speaks of equipment only in general terms, with nothing that fixes a kind, does not satisfy this condition. Where a phrase identifies one particular machine, name the kind that machine belongs to, never what singled that one out.

rules.text: The phrase and its relationship summary show real, concrete involvement with the identified {{entity_noun}}: some party is shown to {{entity_relationships.base}} that {{entity_noun}}, not merely to name, list, or mention it in passing.

It is the manufacturer itself that {{entity_relationships.third_person}} the identified {{entity_noun}} — not a customer, supplier, distributor, or other third party that the manufacturer merely relates to.

children.text: How the manufacturer comes to have the {{entity_noun}} does not matter: direct ownership, leasing, partnership, and access through a parent or sister company all count as the manufacturer itself. The phrase and summary do not have to state who owns it.

sections.heading: A candidate {{entity_noun}} is ruled out if ANY of these guards is violated by it. Ruling out one candidate does not reject the phrase — another candidate may still qualify:

rules.text: The identified {{entity_noun}} has no part in production — it is equipment any business would operate regardless of what, if anything, it makes.
The identified {{entity_noun}} is something the manufacturer sells rather than something it {{entity_relationships.third_person}} — a machine on its product line, not one on its floor.
The manufacturer's use of the identified {{entity_noun}} is only aspirational, hoped-for, planned, on order, or discontinued, rather than current and actual.
